note: Round-3 scout output (10 read-only Sonnet scouts, disjoint surfaces, each dedup'd against register.json's 42 known items). UNAPPROVED candidate list awaiting Owner prioritization. On approval, promoted items move into register.json round3/entries as QUEUED. Priority + live/latent tags + verification are Claude's synthesis, not scout claims. 'verified' = Claude independently confirmed the defect in code this session.
themes: client/server mirror drift is systemic (permissionCatalog, warehouseReconciliationEngine, inventoryAnalytics availableStock) — candidates for a dedicated parity-test workstream
safe-copy error convention (workflowActionErrorMessage/loadErrorMessage) bypassed on 3 more surfaces — one file-disjoint sweep
truncation-without-signal pattern (fixed in coverage #905) recurs in finance AR read

candidates.problem: customerIdentity + useAccountNames/resolveCustomerIdentity were placed inside sibling ScoreBreakdown() (which also references an undefined workOrder), not inside WorkOrderPreview() whose render uses customerIdentity. Undefined-var ReferenceError on render.
candidates.impact: Selecting any Work Order on the Dispatcher Board throws during render — the preview/dispatch pane crashes. Primary dispatcher flow broken.

candidates.problem: Destructures only {data,loading} from useWorkOrders, returns error from technicians read only. Header calls it a known limitation on the stale premise that useWorkOrders has no error callback — #875 already added one; this hook wasn't updated.
candidates.impact: A denied/failed fieldops_wos read renders the Scheduling workspace as a normal empty week instead of its wired FailureState — same false-empty class already fixed elsewhere.

candidates.problem: Server warehouseReconciliationService was hardened by #917 (warehouse-scoped expected qty + fail-closed guard); the client mirror that Operations.jsx actually renders still sums ledger consumption globally and compares to per-warehouse stock, with no guard.
candidates.impact: Live Operations reconciliation panel manufactures spurious HIGH/CRITICAL discrepancies in any multi-warehouse deployment — the exact bug the backend was just fixed to prevent, still shipping in the UI.

candidates.problem: The one deployed inventory-analytics callable builds availableStock from raw physical bin quantity, but generateInventoryHealthDashboard's stockout/urgency math expects reservation-netted availableStock (getAvailableQuantity's warehouseQty - net RESERVED), which every other consumer uses.
candidates.impact: Server callable and the live client dashboard compute different stockout risk/urgency for the same part; server overstates available and understates CRITICAL whenever reservations are outstanding.

candidates.problem: assertValidInput only checks typeof delta === 'number' (NaN/Infinity pass); mergeQtyUsed does Math.max(0, current+delta) with no Number.isFinite guard and no cap vs qtyPlanned. This is the authoritative server write path for qtyUsed (client clamp #887 is separate).
candidates.impact: Any caller (UI bypassable) can persist a NaN or unbounded qtyUsed into inventorySnapshot, corrupting every downstream sum (analytics, COMPLETED consumption) with no error.

candidates.problem: loadFirstPage runs resolveNames() inside the same try as the equipment read; a secondary account/location name-batch failure hits the outer catch which setDocs([]) + denied/error, discarding already-read equipment. loadMore() handles the same call non-destructively (keeps rows, partialError) — proving the correct pattern was known.
candidates.impact: A transient name lookup failure wipes the entire Customer Equipment list and shows a false 'not able to view Equipment' state even though the equipment read succeeded.

candidates.problem: createOpportunity/createSalesOrder got idempotency guards in #893; sibling transitionOpportunity/transitionSalesOrder accept no idempotencyKey and stage no audit replay. Two ADVANCE requests for one intent (retry/double-tap) can each legally advance, skipping a stage. No test for either callable.
candidates.impact: A retried ADVANCE can silently skip a governed pipeline/fulfillment stage with no error and no distinguishing audit trail.

candidates.problem: Pure cores are tested; the five onCall adapters (idempotency replay, required-key guard, capability fail-closed gating, mapCommandError translation) have zero tests. Same gap fixed for coverage in #913, still open in the 'money authority'.
candidates.impact: Duplicate invoices/payments/adjustments/refunds on retry, or an auth-gating bypass, would ship with nothing failing.

candidates.problem: listAccountInvoiceAr reads invoices with .limit(default 100/max 200), no orderBy, no snap.size===limit check, then summarizeAccountAr over the truncated page and returns status 'ready'. Same truncation-without-signal shape fixed in coverage #905.
candidates.impact: An account with more invoices than the page gets openCount/overdue/outstandingByCurrency computed from an arbitrary subset, presented as authoritative — understates real exposure.

candidates.problem: Frontend permissionCatalog is missing 10 backend PermissionIds (all finance.*, coverage.read/write, inventory.catalog.*, inventory.stock.receive) and compatibilityRoles lacks the inventory.stock.receive grant. Hand-mirror 'keep in sync' contract already violated. Distinct from #907 (resolver logic parity).
candidates.impact: findPermission returns undefined client-side for those ids → resolveEffectivePermission previews DENY for authorized principals → any nav/UI visibility preview silently hides authorized functionality. Non-authoritative (not a security bypass) but real drift.

candidates.problem: createTransferOrder validates qty>0 + truthy fields but never checks from!==to. A same (warehouse,bin) transfer makes sourceRef===destRef; both applyLoadedStockDelta tx.set on one doc, last write (+qty) wins, -qty discarded → net +qty from nothing. warehouseServiceTransfer.test only covers distinct bins.
candidates.impact: A trivially-constructible self-transfer fabricates stock in a transaction documented as atomic/correct, corrupting the physical-stock authority and flowing into reconciliation as surplus. Latent until warehouseService is wired to a callable.

candidates.problem: setError(err) passes the raw Firestore onSnapshot error object; TechnicianDashboard and FieldMode render error.message verbatim. Sibling hooks (useCurrentTechnician, useContactsForAccount) wrap via loadErrorMessage.
candidates.impact: Raw Firebase messages ('Missing or insufficient permissions.') shown on the two most-used technician landing screens, violating the app's safe-copy convention.

candidates.problem: advance() surfaces err?.message verbatim in the NextAction failure banner. The identical transitionWorkOrder call in TechnicianWorkOrderActions routes through workflowActionErrorMessage(err); FieldMode never imports it.
candidates.impact: The two surfaces triggering the same governed transition behave inconsistently — Field Mode can show a raw Functions error (possibly with internal ids) on the primary technician screen.

candidates.problem: handleDispatchDrop catch does setDispatchError(err.message), rendered in a role=alert banner. Sibling surfaces (Dispatch.jsx #903, ScheduleWorkOrderForm) use workflowActionErrorMessage; DispatcherBoard never imports it.
candidates.impact: A failed drag-drop dispatch (e.g. double-booking rejection) shows the raw server string incl. internal ids to the dispatcher on the busiest surface.

candidates.problem: Dispatch/Schedule double-booking guard does tx.get(query) for the tech's OTHER WOs then writes only the current WO doc. Two concurrent transitions on different WO docs for the same tech read the same pre-commit snapshot, both see no conflict, both commit — no shared doc forces a retry. Same class as the ledger race; C3 fixed the check, not the concurrency window.
candidates.impact: A tech can be dispatched/scheduled to two occupying WOs simultaneously via the concurrent-request timing window despite the guard.

candidates.problem: triggerInventoryEffects does isStateProcessed() (non-tx read) then markStateProcessed() (separate non-tx write), not wrapped in a shared transaction or lock doc. Two concurrent calls for the same (WO,state) — e.g. retryInventoryEffects tool racing a live call — can both see unprocessed and both run the trigger.
candidates.impact: A double-run of consumeParts writes a second CONSUMED entry (over-consuming), reserve/release similarly double-book; only external sequencing defends it.

candidates.problem: readCurrentState reads the linked Auth user via auth.getUser(...).catch(()=>null) — any error (network/IAM/outage) treated as 'no linked record', unlike the very next getUserByEmail which distinguishes not-found from real errors and rethrows. Masks a real failure past the conflict check into a generic 'Concurrent modification' abort.
candidates.impact: An operator on a transient Auth hiccup gets a misleading 'concurrent modification' error instead of the true cause during a production onboarding run.

candidates.problem: consumeParts always CONSUMES current qtyPlanned, never the outstanding reservation. If qtyPlanned is reduced after DISPATCHED (setWorkOrderPartsPlan, which skips triggerInventoryEffects), outstanding>qtyPlanned, missing goes negative, no top-up, excess RESERVED stranded forever (releaseParts only runs on CANCELLED, which a COMPLETED WO never reaches).
candidates.impact: getAvailableQuantity subtracts the stranded reservation warehouse-wide, permanently understating availability — cumulative unrecoverable drift. Latent: setWorkOrderPartsPlan capability is active:false today.

candidates.problem: deriveArPosition special-cases VOID, but projectInvoiceAr sets outstandingMinor unconditionally (deriveOutstandingMinor ignores state), and summarizeAccountAr keys openCount/outstandingByCurrency off outstandingMinor>0 without checking arPosition. A VOID invoice with residual outstanding is counted as open.
candidates.impact: If any invoice is voided, AR summary overstates open balance with a phantom voided amount. Latent: no governed write path currently sets state=VOID.

candidates.problem: getAvailableQuantity and getOutstandingReservation issue unbounded .where() scans over the append-only inventory_transactions inside every reserve/consume/release transaction — no summary doc, no pagination, no cap.
candidates.impact: Read volume and transaction duration for hot parts grow unboundedly with system age → timeout risk, higher cost, larger lock-contention windows. Structural scalability ceiling in the load-bearing ledger.

candidates.problem: Hand-copies computeAvailableStockByPart justified by a stale comment ('source lives in a React component file') — the function was extracted to domain/inventoryAnalyticsEngine.ts in Sprint 2.1.1 and Operations.jsx now imports it. Third uncoordinated copy of the reservation-netting formula.
candidates.impact: A formula change must be propagated to three places; the justifying comment is factually wrong, misleading the next maintainer.
